MILLBOARD, GREYBOARD AND STRAWBOARD SPECIFICATION --

(Second Revision)

ICS 85.060

0 BIS 2006 BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG NEW DELHI 110002 August 2006 Price Group 7

Paper and Its Products Sectional Committee, CHD 15

FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau ofIndian Standards, afler the drafl finalized by the Paper. and Its Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. This standard was first published in 1964 and subsequently revised in 1967. However, the Sectional Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard decided to revise it further. Changes made in this standard through various amendments have been amalgamated in this revision. Marking clause has also been modified. This standard has been formulated in order to define the quality of mil}board, greyboard and strawboard and to assure the supply of proper quality of such boards to the consumer. In preparing this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from the data made available by various organizations like Government of India Stationery OffIce; the Forest Research Institute & Colleges, Debra Dun and the Chief Inspectorate of Military Explosives, Ministry of Defence, Kirkee where a number of tests were carried out for the purpose. This standard contains clauses 5.4,5 .5,5.7.1 and 6,1 which call for agreement-between the purchaser and the supplier and which permit the purchaser to use his option for selection to suit his requirements. A scheme for Iabelling environment friendly products to be known as ECO Mark has been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEF). The ECO Mark shall be administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, ! 986 as per the Resolution No. 71 dated 20 February 1991, published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible-for ECO Mark i! shall also carry Standard Mark of BIS for quality, in addition to the compliance with the optional environment friendly (EF) requirements. For this purpose, the Standard Mark of BIS would be a single mark being a combination of the 1S1Mark and the ECO logo. Requirements to be satisfied for a product to qualifi for the BIS Standard Mark for ECO friendliness will be included in the relevant Indian Standard. These requirements will be optional; manufacturing units will be tlee to opt for the 1S1Mark alone also. This is based on the Gazette Notification No. 364 dated 7 September 1995 for packaging material/package (Part 1 Paper Board and Plastics excluding laminates) as environment friendly products, published in the Gazette of India. This is, therefore, being issued to this standard to include EF requirements for millboard, greyboard and strawboard. `The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex D. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall +e rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard,

IS 2617:2006

Indian Standard
MILLBOARD, GREYBOARD AND STRAWBOARD SPECIFICATION --

(Second Revision)
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for millboard, greyboard andstrawboard. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. A1l.standardsare subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: lltle IS No. Methods of sampling and test for paper 1060 (Part 1): 1966 and allied products, Part 1 (revised) Methods of sampling and test for paper 1060 (Part 2): 1960 and allied products, Part 2 3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 3.1 Millbowd -- A generic term for a homogeneous board made usually from mixed waste paper on an intermittent board machine, generally in thickness greater than 1 mm. 3.1.1 Mixed WastePaper -- Pieces of paper or board that may be reclaimed after use or from a converting process -forre-pulping and making again into paper or board. 3.1.2 Intermittent Machine -- A machine for forming sheets of board. It consists of either a fourdrinier former or one or more cylinder moulds or vats. The wet web is wound on a drum forming a continuous mat of several layers. When the required thickness is obtained, this sheet is cut and stripped from the drum. 3.2 7Meyboard -- A homogeneous board made usually of mixed waste payers with or without screenings and mechanical pulp on a continuous board machine, in thickness not greater than 1 mm. 3.3 Strawboard -- Board made tlom partially cooked straw, grass, bagasse or other agricultural residues or mixture of these. 3.4 Grammage -- Mass of paper or board in grams per square metre after conditioning under standard atmospheric conditions of 27 * 2�C temperature and 65* 2 percent relative humidity. 4 GRADES Millboard and strawboard shall be of two grades, namely, Grade A and Grade B while greyboard shall only be of one grade. 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 General The boards shall be uniform in thickness and shall lie flat. Both sides of the board shall be clean and flee from loosely bound tibres. 5.2 Slitting and Cutting Sheets shall be cut clean and square to specified dimensions. All cut edges shall be free from loose fibres and dust. 5.2.1 Tolerance on Squareness The tolerance on squarenessshall be such that the shorter diagonal of the sheet shall not differ from the longer by more than 1percent of the former. 5.3 Tolerance on Thickness When tested in accordance with 7 of IS 1060 (Part 1), a tolerance of +10 percent shall be allowed on the average thickness. 5.4 Grammage and Tolerance on Grammage The nominal grammage of millboard, greyboard, and strawboard shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. A tolerance of + 5 percent shall be allowed on the nominal gramrntige, when tested in accordance with 6 of IS 1060 (Part 1). 5.5 Sizes and Tolerance on Sizes The sizes of the board shall be as agreed to between the

1S 2617:2006 purchaser and.the supplier. The tolerance on the sizes shall be+ 0.5 percent of the ordered measurement. Where 0.5 percent is less than 3 mm, the tolerance shall be + 3 mm; and where 0.5 percent exceeds 6 mm, the tolerance shall be + 6 mm when tested in accordance with 4.3.1 of IS 1060 (Part 1). 5.6 Millboard shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1 when tested according to the relevant test methods given in CO1 5, 6 and 7 of Table 1. 5.7 Greyboard shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 2 when tested according to the relevant test methods given in COI4 and 5 of Table 2. 5.7.-1 If agreed to%etween the purchaser and the supplier, greyboard shall also pass the cupping test prescribed in Annex B of this standard. 5.8 Strawboard shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 3 when tested according to the relevant test methods given in CO1 5,6 and 7 of Table 3. 5.9 Additional Requirements for ECO Mark
5.9.1 General Requirements 5.9.1.1

The product shall conform to the requirements for quality and performance prescribed under 5.1 to 5.8.
5.9.1.2

The manufacturer shall produce to BIS, the environmental consent clearance from the concerned State Pollution Control Board as per provisions of Water (Prwention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and Air (Prevention and Control ofPol/ution)Act, 1981 along with the authorization, if required under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the Rules made thereunder,

5.9.2 Specific Requirements 5:9.2.1 The material shall be of the following two types depending on the raw material used in the manufacture:

IS 2617:2006 a) Type A � Manufactured from pulp containing not less than 60 percent by mass of pulp made from materials other than bamboo, hardwood, softwood and reed. b) ~pe B � Manufactured from pulp made from 100 percent waste paper or agricultural/industrial waste. 5.9.2.2 The material, if used for the packaging of food materials, shall be manufactured from virgin pulp and shall be free from dioxins. Printed surfaces of the paper shall not come into contact with the food and the maximum amounts of contaminants in paper intended to come into contact with food shall not.exceed the limits prescribed in Table 4 when tested according to the methods given in Annex C. 6 PACKING AND MARKING
6.1 Packing

6.2.2 BIS Certt~cation Marking Each package may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 6.2.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau oflndian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder, The details of conditions under which the Iicence for the use of the Standard Mark maybe granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6.3 Additirmd Requirements
for ECO Mark

6.3.1 For ECO Mark, millboard, greyboard and strawboard

shall be packed in such packages which~hall be recyclable/ reusable or biodegradable. 6.3.2 The -millboard, greyboard and strawboard may display in brief-the criteria based on which the product has been labelled as environment Iiiendly. 6.3.3 The milIboard, greyboard and strawboard shall be sold along with instruction for proper use and mode of safe disposal so as to maximize its performance and minimize wastage. 6.3.4 It shall be suitably marked that ECO Mark label is applicable only to the millboard,.greyboard and strawboard if content is not separately covered under the ECO Mark scheme. NOTEIt maybe stated that the ECO Mark is applicable to the productor packaging material or both.

The board shall be securely and suitably packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 6.2 Marking
6.2.1 Each package shaIl be marked with the following

particulars: a) Description of the material; b) Grammage in g/m2; c) Thickness in microns and size of sheet; d) Number of sheets (in the package) and net weight of the contents; -e) Batch number o Month and year of manufacture; and k) Name of manufacturer and trade-mark, if any.

ANNEX

A

[S/ No. (iv) of Tables 1,2 and 3]
METHOD FOR TESTING STIFFNESS

A-1 APPARATUS

The apparatus shall consist of the following: a) A sample holder in which the test piece may be clamped; b) A means of applying acontrolled bending moment to the portion of the test piece protruding horn the clamp, the moment arm being 10 mm in length; and c) Suitable scales on which are indicated simultaneously, the angular deflection of the moment arm, and the bending moment applied. A-2 TEST PIECES Representative test pieces, 15 mm wide and about 50 mm long, shall be cut from the sample in both the machine and cross directions. A-3 PROCEDURE

5 degrees in 5 s. Note the value of the bending moment and release the load. Repeat the operation three or four times. Record the average bending moment for the test piece in gram-centimetre for a 5 degrees deflection in 5s; neglecting the first reading. A-3.2 Cut the next test piece in the same direction but deflect it in the opposite sense, that is, towards or away from the front side as the case may be. Test at least four test pieces in each sense t?om the machine direction and an equal number from the cross direction. A-3.3 Calculate the bending moment in the machine and cross directions separately and report the average stitl%ess values for the machine and cross directiorwof the sample. A-3.4 The value may alsobe expressed as stiffness factor as follows: Average stifiess Stiffness factor = lot3 where t = thickness in mm.

ANNEX

B

[S/ No. (vii), Table 1 and Clause 5.7.1] CUPPING TEST

B-1 GEN-ERAL This test is applicable for millboard. B-2 PROCEDURE B-2.1 Cut out a disc from each test piece. Damp the disc by dipping momentarily in water and then air dry for 5 to

10min till all surface moisture is removed but the millboard remains just damp, Then press the disc into a cup-shaped mould of diameter approximately 76 mm to form a cup 12.5 mm deep. The radius of curvature at the circular edge of the plunger, which shall be rounded off, shall be 6 mm. B-2, 1.1 The cup so produced must be tlee from chipping and cracks at the bottom where the material is turned up.

One millilitre of this solution contains 500 ~g of chromium (as Cr b+). C-1.3.6 Intermediate Chromium Solution -- Take 10 ml of stock chromium solution and dilute to 1 000 ml with distilled water. One millilitre of this solution contains 5.00 pg of chromium (as Cr 6+). C-2 DETERMINATION
C-2.1 Principle
mxD

OF MERCURY (as Hg)

The flameless atomic absorption procedure is a physical method based on the absorption of radiation at 253.7 am by mercury vapour. The mercury is reduced to the elemental state and aerated from solution in a closed system. The mercury vapour passes through a cell positioned in the light path of mercury hallow cathode lamp of an atomic absorption spectrophotometer. Absorbance (peak height) is measured as a fimction of mercury concentration and record. C-2.2 Apparatus C-2.2.1 Atonric Absorption Spectrometer (AAS) and Associated Equipment -- Instrument settirtgs recommended by the manufacturer shall be followed. Instruments designed specifically for the measurement of mercury using the cold vapour technique may be substituted for the AAS. C-2.2.2 Mercury Vapour Generation Assembly -- Consistsof an absorption cell, peristaltic pump, flow meter, 7

C-4.1 Principle OF CADMKJM-(as Cd)

The cadmium content of the sample is determined by electrothermal atomic absorption spectrometric method. C-4.2 Apparatus

C-3.4.1

Sample Preparation
C-4.2.1

Tear the air dry sample into pieces of suitable size. Do not use cut or punched edges or other parts where metallic contamination may have occurred. C-3.4.2 Preparation of Test Solution Weigh to the nearest 0,01 g about 20 g of paper, leach-the paper with about 200 ml of extraction fluid for 18*2 h using shaker rotating/moving at 30 * 2 rev/rein. Filter the extract through glass fibre filter with 0,45 micron pore size. C-3.4.3 Transfer the extract to a 250 ml conical flask. Add 5 ml concentrate nitric acid and a few boiling chips or glass beads. Slowly evaporate on a hot plate to about 10 to 20 ml. Continue heating and adding concentrated nitric acid until digestion is complete. Wash down with water and then filter if necessary. Quantitati~ely transfer filtrate to a 100 ml volumetric flask, dilute to the mark and mix thoroughly. C-3.4.4 Inject a measuredportion of the digested solution into the graphhe oven. Dry, char and atomize accortlng to the preset programme. Measure the absorbance. C-3.4.5 Prepare a reagent blank and sufllcient standards containing 5.0, 7.5 and 10.0 mg/1 of lead by diluting suitable volume of the standard lead solution with nitric acid (1.: 499) and repeat as above (see C-3.4.3). Inject a suitable portion of each standard solution in order of 9

C-5 DETERMINATION
PHENOL (PCP) C-5.1 Principle

OF PENTACHLORO-

C-4.4.1 Sample Preparation Tear the air dry sample into pieces of suitable size. Do not use cut or punched edges or other parts where metallic contamination may have occurred.
C-4.4.2

PCP is extracted with acetone by Soxhlet extraction. Acetone extract is evaporated to dryness and subjected to acetylation. The acetylated PCP is determined quantitatively by Gas Chromatograph- Electron Capture Detector (GC.ECD). C-5.2 Apparatus
C-5.2.1

Preparation of Test Solution

Weigh to the nearest 0.01 g about 20 g of paper, leach the paper with about 200 ml of extraction fluid for 18+2 h using shaker rotating/moving at 30 + 2 rev/rein. Filter the extract through glass tibre filter with 035 micron pore size. C-4.4.3 Transfer the extract to a 250 ml conical flask. Add 5 ml concentrate nitric acid and a few boiling chips or glass beads. Slowly evaporate on a hot plate to about 10 to 20 ml. Continue heating and adding concentrated nitric acid until digestion is complete. Wash down with distilled water and then filter if necessary. Quantitatively transfer filtrate to a 100 ml volumetric flask, dilute to the mark and mix thoroughly. C-4.4.4 Inject a measured portion of the digested solution into the graphite oven. Dry, char and atomize according to the preset programme. Measure the absorbance. C-4.4.5 Prepare a reagent blank and sufficient standards containing 5.0, 7.5 and 10.0 mg/1of cadmium by diluting suitable volume of the standard cadmium solution with nitric acid (1 : 499). Inject a suitable portion of each standard solution in order of increasing concentration. Analyze each standard solution and measure the absorbance.

C-5.2.6 Gas Chromatography with ECD -- capillary Cohnnns. C-5.2.7 Glass Columns -- Length 20 cm, internal diameter 12 mm filled with 5 cm of silica gel having particle size 63 pm x 200 ym. C-6 DETERMINATION BIPHENYLS (PCBS) C-6.1 Principle

OF POLYCHLORINATED

Clean Up

Transfer the extract (see C-5.4.2) to the silica gel packed column and elute with about 25 ml of n-hexane at the rate of 2 ml/min. Collect the eluent in a flask. Dry over anhydrous sodium sulphate and evaporte nearly to dryness. C-5.4.4 Treat the residue (see C-5.4.3) with 1ml of acetic anhydride, and heat on a water bath for about 30 rein, Remove the flask from the water bath and cool the acetylated product. Transfer the content in a separating fimnel and add 10 mi of hexane and 5 ml distilled water. Shake well for2 min and let the layers be separated. Collect the hexane layer, dry over anhydrous sodium sulphate and evaporate nearly to dryness. Cool for at least 10 rein, add 1 m 1 of internal standard solution and adjust the volume to 5.0 ml with n-hexane. C-5.4.5 Inject 2 p] of the solution into the Gas Chromatography.Record the peak size in area and peak height units. If peak response exceeds linear range of the system, dilute the concentration of the extract and re-analyze. C-5.4.6 Calibration Prepare three calibration standards fkomthe PCP standard solutions.Add 1ml of internal standard solution and follow the steps as above (see C-5.4.3 to C-5.4.5). Tabulate peak height or area responses against calculated equivalent mass of underivatized pentachlorophenol injected. Prepare a calibration curve. Standards

BIS k a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking ~d quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course.of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to -copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. .Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
